Do we see reality as it is?

The bit about the desktop definitely helps make his point, that we don't construct reality, rather reconstruct reality. I will talk about what I got from this.

He studies competitive organisms in an environment with different traits. It is pretty intuitive that organisms trained for "fitness," (the ability to recognize something beneficial in the moment) have the edge in evolution. For example, it is pleasurable to engage in eating good food, while painful to experience cold weather. An activity is only pleasurable or painful depending on whether we percieve it to help us survive. In regard to the beetle he mentioned. Yes, it survived not because it recognized reality, but because it recognized characteristics of a suitable female. Yes, humans survived not because they recognized reality, but because they recognized suitable traits in other humans, (big breast size, large muscles, but mostly unique to primates, we selected for social characteristics as well.)

These social characteristics were allowed to become more complex through a bigger, more complex brain. This in turn, allowed for more complex social interaction. It can be assumed that a more complex social interaction is beneficial because we are able to engage in implied social contracts, that is to say, expected behavior. For example, if I introduce myself, you are expected to introduce yourself. From that point, we can discuss how we can help each other. Helping eachother benefits us both mutually, which allows for us to survive. This is a typical interaction. If I were to introduce myself, and you stood there, the situation would be awkward. Non-awkward behavior allows for quick beneficial social interaction.

My point in all this is that although his studies select for fitness, we as humans are unique in our ability to form the most complex interactions and utilize the most complex tools, that help us percieve reality more accurately. So to answer the original question, what is conciousness and how does it come about, will probably be answered when we create it ourselves. So now that I explained what factually seperates humans from other animals, (their ability to use complicated tools/complicated social interaction) I wanted to discuss what I believe might be happening when neurons are activated in the occipital lobe. A digital camera takes light and focuses it via the lens onto a sensor made out of silicon. It is made up of a grid of tiny photosites that are sensitive to light. Each photosite is usually called a pixel, a contraction of "picture element". There are millions of these individual pixels in the sensor of a DSLR camera.

The eye does not equal a camera in any traditional sense, (refer to this vsauce https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4I5Q3UXkGd0) and we should not assume it works like a digital camera. The neurons are doing image processing to form an image that your brain believes to be accurate. This can be demonstrated in many ways that highlight the shortcomings of the human eye. That said, do we construct or reconstruct reality? Reconstruct. Is it as drastic a difference as he made it out to be. No I don't think so. So I disagree with the speaker. I don't think that with all the confirmation and verification we get through our tools is so far off that it has prevented us from answering what the relationship is between your brain and your experience. What has prevented us is that it is so damn complex! There are over a trillion connections in your brain. http://www.human-memory.net/brain_neurons.html

We will eventually understand the relationship between patterns of connections and consciousness just as we have mapped the human genome. They are both tasks that are hugely complicated but will with time be solved.
